title: Systems Approach Explained Simply | Principles of Management Ep 12
description:
Why does one broken cash counter stop a whole chai stall? In this animated lesson, Chai Corner has six people, and when Kabir's counter fails, the kitchen and the cleaning suffer too. That is the systems approach in action.

You will learn where the systems approach came from (Ludwig von Bertalanffy's general systems theory, picked up by management thinkers in the 1950s and 1960s), what subsystems are, the input, process (transformation), output and feedback loop, what an open system is (customers, suppliers, government and competitors), and synergy: the whole is greater than the sum of its parts.

This is Episode 12 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 One broken counter, a whole stall in trouble
0:19 Not six jobs, one system
0:24 What is the systems approach?
0:52 Subsystems
1:08 Inputs, process, outputs and feedback
1:32 An open system
1:47 Synergy
2:00 Quick check
2:14 Recap
